- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3), model often underestimates upside — add 3–7% buffer to forecast for next 5 days.  
- Model frequently underestimates short-term volatility in sentiment-driven markets — increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 1–3 day horizons.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to ignore sentiment momentum — weight recent sentiment (last 5 days) 30% more than historical average in smoothing.
